snapshot_note: v0.53.0 released on develop 2026-07-26 - `-static-libmadc` now works in the .o LINK lane, lifting forest-carriers S5's last stated boundary. The AOT ledger is carried as MIR modules, so the pieces a program needs are pulled into a PRIVATE object-mode context, generated, emitted with MIR_gen_object_emit, and merged into the same builder as the .o inputs. Through the merge deliberately: a builder's symbol table is append-only (MIR_object_add_symbol never dedupes by name), and the unification that turns the inputs' UNDEF entries into references to the runtime's definitions IS the merge - so the runtime rides the ONE unification implementation, on the read-back path both containers (ELF ET_REL and MH_OBJECT) already gate. No new format code, no fork change. Generalized rather than duplicated: cir_ledger_pull takes a SEED list (the builder's UNDEF names join the module imports under the same not-defined filter), and the cover analysis takes the reference LIST rather than its source (source lanes pass context imports, the .o lane passes MIR_object_undef_name) - same classifier, same two diagnostics. Fixed on the way: the AOT-ledger carrier now opens HEADER-ONLY (the ledger is a container-global segment, but the probe ran complete_open, which binds the frozen string pool and arena into LIVE parse state - it died with 'forest thaw requires a live string pool' in a lane with no lexer). New -fno-eval-shims: every .o carries __madc_shim_* host-call adapters whose twelve madc_value_* imports are Tier B, an executable emit from source skips them and a .o cannot know, so the build says it (the -fPIC shape). Fork unchanged (1.0-madc.0.52.0 @ba216dea).

live_handoff: SESSION 2026-07-27 #16: P2.0 `-stdlib=` SHIPPED — a C++ standard library is now a selectable FLAVOR, and selecting one REPLACES the include search list. Branch feature/libcxx-flavor-claude @e114cbae, NOT merged, NOT released. Read this, then docs/plans/2026-07-26-libcxx-flavor-plan.md (its "Worklist status" table is the actionable list). === 1. WHAT LANDED @e114cbae. A search list is a property of the standard library, not an ordering preference, so gen_sys_includes.sh now emits ONE TABLE PER FLAVOR — madc_stdlib_flavors[] of { name, paths, compiler_owned_dir } in the generated src/sys_include_paths.cpp — and -stdlib= picks between them. That is what clang's driver does: one list built per library, not one list reordered. The resource dir is per-flavor too, because gcc's and clang's differ and it is the slot madc's embedded freestanding set occupies in the search order. THE MOTIVATING FAILURE, now a passing gate leg: std::string under libc++ died in /usr/include/c++/13/stdlib.h on `using std::abort;`, because libc++'s <cstdlib> reaches the C library through `#include_next <stdlib.h>` and, with the GNU C++ dirs still on the path behind libc++, that walk lands on GNU's wrapper. -I can put a library FIRST; first is not the same as ONLY. === 2. THREE PROPERTIES OF THE DESIGN, keep them. (a) WHICH FLAVORS EXIST IS A BUILD-HOST FACT, DISCOVERED, NEVER LISTED. The default is whatever $(CXX) resolves to; an alternate is recorded when a probe reports a DIFFERENT library. The candidate probe commands ($(CXX) -stdlib=..., clang++-18 -stdlib=libc++, ...) are tool SPELLINGS, not answers — each is asked what it actually resolved to by reading the library's own _LIBCPP_VERSION / __GLIBCXX__, so a candidate whose compiler or library is absent reports nothing and drops out. The `!= default` test is what makes a silent fallback impossible to mistake for a second flavor. MADC_STDLIB_ALT_CXX overrides discovery. (b) ONE READER. All five consumers — the lexer's <...> resolution, is_system_header_path, #include_next, and the two embedded-header partition predicates — now go through Program::sys_include_paths() / compiler_owned_include_dir(), which also collapsed three copies of the no-compiler fallback list into one. Deleting the old globals let the compiler confirm the sweep was complete. Two of those sites previously skipped the fallback entirely; centralizing gives it to them, which only changes behaviour on a host with no compiler to probe, and in the correct direction. (c) AN UNAVAILABLE FLAVOR FAILS LOUD, naming what THIS BINARY was built with — because availability is a property of the machine that built it, a diagnostic listing the flag's possible spellings would be useless. Bare `-stdlib=` is rejected too (it must not match an unnamed entry on a compiler-less build host). === 3. REACHABLE FROM ALL THREE SURFACES a flavor can arrive on: -stdlib= on the CLI; `stdlib =` in madc.ini (CLI wins, same precedence as `std`); and -stdlib= in a compile_commands.json entry — that last one because a libc++ project's manifest carries it and IGNORING IT WOULD SILENTLY COMPILE AGAINST THE WRONG LIBRARY'S HEADERS. === 4. THE NEXT BLOCKER, with a two-line reducer and six hypotheses already ELIMINATED. std::string under -stdlib=libc++ now reaches deep into libc++ and stops at c++/v1/cctype:111, `using ::isalnum;`. Reducer: `#include <string_view>` then `#include <cwchar>`. ELIMINATED BY MEASUREMENT (do not re-test): include resolution/#include_next (the -v trace shows the exact clang chain cctype -> c++/v1/ctype.h -> /usr/include/ctype.h, so glibc's header IS read); PCH divergence (zero `precompiled` hits in that trace); inline namespaces (`namespace std { inline namespace __1 { using ::isalnum; } }` compiles); #undef dropping the function (`#define isalnum(c) 0` then `#undef isalnum` then `using ::isalnum;` compiles); <string_view> poisoning global lookup (<string_view>+<ctype.h>+using compiles, and so does <string_view>+<cctype>); and every header alone (<cctype>, <cwctype>, <__string/char_traits.h>, <string_view>, <stdexcept> all compile). So it needs <cwchar> SPECIFICALLY plus a prior header — <cwchar> alone gets PAST cctype and fails later at its own cwchar:202, a `std::wcslen` CALL, a different construct with a different diagnostic. And note <string_view> already pulls <cwchar> transitively, so the explicit second include should be a guard-skip no-op yet changes the outcome. THAT is the thread: parse/registration state, not which file was opened. === 5. A PROBE TRAP THAT COST ME AN HOUR, recorded because it will recur. `isalnum(65)` COMPILES UNDER MADC WHETHER OR NOT isalnum IS DECLARED — the implicit-function/dlsym fallback accepts it. An early probe used exactly that and I concluded "the ctype chain works standalone", which was not what the probe measured. PROBE A DECLARATION WITH `using ::X;`, NEVER WITH A CALL. This is the same class as the `(int)std::is_same<>::value` cast trap from session #15: suspect the probe before theorizing about the subject. === 6. EVIDENCE. Full battery at the pre-final build: JIT 760 passed / 0 failed / 0 timed out / 9 skipped; EXE 744/0; OBJ 744/0. fulltest's only failure was scripts/forest_config_gate.sh asserting the schema's accepted-key list literally — adding the madc.ini `stdlib` key moved it. Both tests that pin that list (tests/unit/test_config_file.cpp and the gate) were updated; the duplication is deliberate, they pin one contract at two layers, and loosening either to make a schema change cheaper is the wrong trade. After the two post-battery source edits (the bare-`-stdlib=` guard and the empty-flavor-list diagnostic) I rebuilt and re-ran ONLY what those edits can reach: forest_config_gate OK, libcxx_gate OK on all 10 legs, test_config_file 19/19 cases 88/88 assertions, plus manual checks that bare `-stdlib=` is rejected with the flavor list and that `stdlib = libc++` in madc.ini works end-to-end. Those two edits live in functions no test reaches without passing -stdlib=, which is the named boundary for not re-running the battery. === 7. NEXT, in priority order. (a) The cctype blocker in §4 — the reducer is two lines, start from the guard-skip observation. (b) is_destructible evaluates wrong, which is what makes is_trivially_destructible wrong; madc's own __has_trivial_destructor is CORRECT (1/0/1 matching g++), so the defect is upstream in the SFINAE/declval chain — the real tsubst burn-down. (c) &S::n still reports "Unknown namespace 'S'" (parseAddressOfExpression, a different function from the one fixed @3167da3c). === 8. A CONFLATION FOUND AND DELIBERATELY LEFT ALONE. cir_native_link_env() in src/madc_cir.cpp picks the C++ runtime for DT_NEEDED — libc++ vs libstdc++.so.6 — behind a host `#ifdef __APPLE__`. That is the platform-means-library conflation this whole track exists to undo, and it is doubly confused: the #ifdef is a property of the machine madc was BUILT on while DT_NEEDED describes the TARGET. It works today only because the two happen to agree. It belongs to the P2.3 flavor switch; written up in the plan doc's P2.3 section rather than fixed here, because the native link lane is a different surface than P2.0's. === 9. VLA NOT DEALLOCATED ON BACKWARD GOTO: a `goto` jumping back to before a VLA's declaration must deallocate the VLA (gcc/C semantics; gcc-torture 20040811-1.c). madc lowers VLAs as malloc + __attribute__((cleanup)), which frees only on SCOPE EXIT, not on the backward goto re-entering the scope — so a backward-goto loop over a VLA LEAKS one allocation per iteration. 20040811-1.c leaks ~2GB over 1e6 iterations; it passes only when memory is available (it OOM-SIGSEGV'd when the MIR fork's 128MB code-holder reservation reduced headroom — see mir_fork; arch-gated off x86-64, so it passes again). Proper fix: free the VLA at the backward goto. Separate future slice.
